title: Reading data back
summary: How a chart or table in the portal gets its rows. Laravel authorizes the request and adds the organization and its retention; the runtime runs the SQL. The portal polls: the server-sent telemetry stream exists only for integration applications.

boxes.label: Portal chart or table
boxes.detail: Dashboard panels re-read latest values at the dashboard's refresh rate and history for relative ranges, with at most four telemetry requests in flight. The device page re-reads latest values every five seconds. Charts ask for 500 points.

boxes.label: DeviceController
boxes.detail: Routes under /api/v1/organizations/{organization}/devices/{device}/measurements sit behind Sanctum and the organization context. Each method checks that the device belongs to the organization and that the person holds Device.view there, then validates the range and limits.

boxes.label: DeviceReadings
boxes.detail: Shared by the portal's endpoints, the agent tools and applications' history and records. It adds the organization, the device and the organization's effective retention days, and for charts asks for observed time with configuration revisions merged. Every reading it returns from history, records, state history or increase carries recorded_in.

boxes.label: RuntimeClient
boxes.detail: Calls the runtime with the shared token. Range reads wait 30 seconds, longer than the runtime's own 25-second limit, so its explanation arrives instead of a dropped connection. A 422 becomes a validation error, a 504 is passed on, anything else failing is a 503.

boxes.label: Integration API
boxes.detail: Applications read the devices their grant covers. Latest values, a batch of them for up to 100 devices, and the stream go straight to RuntimeClient. History and records go through DeviceReadings like the portal's, but history keeps the runtime's default: receipt time, one series per configuration.

boxes.label: Readings before a move
boxes.detail: A moved device's range reads continue into its predecessors: one whose move shared its readings, earlier moves included, or one that was in the device's own organization. Laravel asks the runtime once more for each part, under the organization that recorded it, its retention and its parameter, up to the cutover, then joins the answers oldest first. recorded_in is self for the device's own organization and source for another; the runtime never reads across organizations.

boxes.label: Refused or failed
boxes.detail: The portal shows the message it is given. A 504 says the range has too many readings to load in time; a 422 from history says the range holds too many values or configuration changes.

boxes.label: Runtime internal HTTP
boxes.sub: Checks the token, clamps the range
boxes.detail: Every /internal/ request needs the bearer token. Range reads move from up to the retention cutoff and to down to now, and run in a read-only transaction with a 25-second statement limit instead of the pool's 5 seconds.

boxes.label: Latest values
boxes.detail: Reads each parameter's row, preferring the applied configuration and carrying a value over from the previous one while type and unit match. Good values are then marked stale when they predate activation, when no compatible source session is online or when the parameter's freshness interval has passed. A device the runtime no longer serves returns its retained values as inactive. Retention does not apply.

boxes.label: Bucketed history
boxes.sub: avg, min, max, count per bucket
boxes.detail: Numbers are grouped into buckets of range ÷ (max_points ÷ 2) seconds, at least one second, each with average, minimum, maximum and count. Other types return every value. A valueless point marks where a series stopped reporting, so the chart breaks its line. More than 2000 points is an error, not a truncated answer. bucket_seconds replaces the derived width, so the reads of a moved device and its predecessors share bucket edges; it may be up to a year and must not give more than max_points buckets.

boxes.label: Raw records
boxes.detail: Observation rows newest first by received_at, 50 a page by default and at most 100, up to a limit of 500 by default and at most 5000. The cursor is signed with the runtime token and tied to the query, so it cannot be reused for another one. For a moved device Laravel continues the pages into the earlier parts, newest first, with a cursor of its own and the same limit.

boxes.label: State and counters
boxes.detail: State history returns only the changes of a boolean, enum or colour parameter, starting from the last value before the range, with the time spent in each state. Counter increase sums the growth per calendar bucket (15m to 1y) in an IANA time zone and treats a decrease as a rollover or a reset. Both order by observed time.

boxes.label: Telemetry stream
boxes.detail: For up to 1000 devices: open, then reading frames whose ID is the outbox sequence. A resumed stream is caught up from telemetry_outbox 500 rows a page, then fed live by the committed relay. A position older than anything retained gets reset; a subscriber more than 1000 events behind is closed and resumes. Laravel relays the frames and rechecks the grant.

steps.text: A panel asks for latest values or a time range through the API client. Nothing is pushed to the portal: panels ask again on a timer.
A device in another organization is a 404, and a person without Device.view is a 403. Nothing reaches the runtime.

The validated request goes to DeviceReadings, which adds the organization, the device and its retention days. Charts also ask for observed time, so a backlog uploaded late appears when it was measured.
If the device was moved, the same read is repeated for each earlier part of its history, under the organization that recorded it, and the answers are joined. Every reading says where it was recorded.
RuntimeClient calls the runtime's internal endpoint with the shared bearer token. The runtime clamps the range to the retention cutoff and to now.
Latest values come from the latest table, then are downgraded to stale or inactive from what the runtime knows about the device right now.
A chart with 500 points gets at most 250 buckets of average, minimum, maximum and count, plus markers where the series stopped.
The records table pages through observation rows by receipt time with a signed cursor.
State timelines and counter consumption are computed in SQL over observed time.
A range that is too broad returns 422, a query cut off at 25 seconds returns 504 and unavailable storage returns 503. Laravel passes the message on.
Integration applications read the devices their grant covers: history and records through DeviceReadings, latest values straight through the same client.
Only they get a live stream: stored readings as server-sent events, resumable from a position in the committed outbox.
